content.text:
Investigation complete. The grant in § 13 satisfies every **preferred** element, reinforced by § 24.1 and § 30.5, with no at-will revocation or suspension right anywhere in the document.

- **Affiliates** — p0054 and p0055 both grant to "Customer and its Affiliates"; § 30.5 preserves Affiliate enforcement rights. No written-notice or Affiliate-order gating in § 4 or § 2.
- **Contractors** — p0054 grants to "contractors acting on their behalf"; p0055 permits contractors to support paid-up material.
- **Perpetual / irrevocable paid-up licence** — p0055; § 14.3 extends it to embedded Vendor Technology; § 10.1 confirms paid-up licences survive termination.
- **Revocation only for uncured material breach** — p0056 limits revocation/suspension to a "material uncured payment or use breach ... after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure" (narrower than any material breach). § 9 gives Vendor no at-will termination; § 7.3 bars suspension during payment disputes; § 24.4 bars suspension on change of control.
- **Successor transfer** — p0056 plus § 24.1 (consent-free assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor).

No redline is warranted — this clause already exceeds our fallback.

input.quote: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: The licence grant meets the preferred position in full, so no redline is needed. § 13.1 grants the subscription right directly to Customer, its Affiliates and "contractors acting on their behalf" — no written-notice or Affiliate-order gating exists in § 2 or § 4, and § 30.5 expressly preserves enforcement rights for a Customer Affiliate and a permitted successor. § 13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, extended to embedded Vendor Technology by § 14.3 and confirmed to survive termination by § 10.1. On revocability, § 13.3 permits revocation or suspension only "during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure" — narrower than the preferred "uncured material breach" standard and therefore better for us; Vendor has no at-will termination right (§ 9.1 requires a thirty-day uncured material breach; § 9.4 without-cause termination is Customer's alone), § 7.3 requires Services to continue during a payment dispute, and § 24.4 bars suspension on our change of control. Transferability is satisfied by § 13.3 read with § 24.1, which permits assignment without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets. § 13.4 use restrictions and § 12 do not narrow the grant. This sits above the fallback, at the preferred position.
